description:
Olivine stages page mutations but some operations read only the pre-batch index. Consequently later mutations do not consistently observe earlier mutations in the same ordered stream. Commit proxies combine successful client transactions into a per-log mutation stream, so the defect also affects different transactions placed in one batch.

Confirmed at `8f962e09` using `Transaction.encode/1` -> `IndexManager.apply_transaction/3` -> index/value lookup.

## Minimal reproduction

Run as an `.exs` file with `MIX_ENV=test mix run --no-start /tmp/repro.exs`:

```elixir
alias Bedrock.DataPlane.{Transaction, Version}
alias Bedrock.DataPlane.Materializer.Olivine.{Database, IndexManager, Index}
path = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "mutation-order-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}")
File.mkdir_p!(path)
{:ok, db} = Database.open(:mutation_order_repro, Path.join(path, "db"))
encoded = Transaction.encode(%{
  commit_version: Version.from_integer(100),
  mutations: [
    {:atomic, :add, "counter", <<1>>},
    {:atomic, :add, "counter", <<1>>},
    {:set, "newkey", "value"},
    {:clear_range, "new", "newz"}
  ]
})
{im, db} = IndexManager.apply_transaction(IndexManager.new(), encoded, db)
[{_, {index, _}} | _] = im.versions
{:ok, _, loc} = Index.locator_for_key(index, "counter")
IO.inspect(Database.load_value(db, loc)) # actual {:ok, <<1>>}; expected <<2>>
IO.inspect(Index.locator_for_key(index, "newkey")) # actual :ok; expected :not_found
Database.close(db)
File.rm_rf!(path)
```

## Cause

[lib/bedrock/data_plane/materializer/olivine/index_update.ex](https://github.com/bedrock-kv/bedrock/blob/8f962e09b24765265eeb6bd818f5b26da8d91b99/lib/bedrock/data_plane/materializer/olivine/index_update.ex#L251) computes atomics through `get_current_value_for_atomic_op/3`, which looks at `index_update.index` rather than pending writes. Each result then overwrites the same pending entry. Range clears similarly enumerate the pre-batch pages and miss keys newly staged by earlier sets.

This is distinct from the inclusive-end clear bug: `newkey` is strictly inside `[new,newz)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Compare ordered mutation sequences against an independent sequential reference interpreter.
- Cover add+add, set+atomic, clear+atomic, set+clear_range, clear_range+set, and operations crossing page splits.
- Include a real commit-proxy batch containing separate client transactions targeting the same key.
- Verify equivalent values after persistence and replay.

No change proposed here. Ordering oracle deliberately uses nonoverflowing one-byte additions.
